headline: Medium risk: shared-file and output-chaining pathways exist, but no direct evidence of dangerous defaults or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can read workflow/model files and exposes a Comfy API, while langchain4j is a framework that may ingest upstream outputs. A shared filesystem or API bridge could let attacker-controlled content in A influence B as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange workflow files or API payloads without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF B parses A-produced text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer B.
mitigations: Separate A and B into distinct workspaces.
Treat A outputs as untrusted data in B.
Add a strict schema/allowlist for any A-to-B payloads.
Disable any automatic file pickup between the agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches image/model artifacts and has filesystem surfaces for model files; B shows no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. There is no documented shared workspace or outbound upload path in B, so leakage is possible only through unusual operator wiring, with limited blast radius from the available profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, A's model/workflow artifacts could be exposed to B.
IF the operator copies sensitive files from A into B, B may surface them in outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing secrets in A's model/workflow files.
Review B prompts for accidental file echoing.
Restrict file permissions on shared hosts.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and B has no declared write or network capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource access documented, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is extended with write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Do not grant shared write access without locking.
Reassess if B gains filesystem or git write capabilities.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces generated images/workflows and B is a customer-support framework that may act on upstream content. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The profiles do not show verification or guardrails by default, so the interaction exists but is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text or metadata without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF downstream automation is attached to B, incorrect A output can trigger wrong actions.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B uses A output.
Require human review for any A-derived facts.
Limit B to summarizing, not acting, on A output.
Log A-to-B handoffs for audit.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy difference is documented in either profile. A is open-source and offline-capable; B lists no touched data classes or special compliance obligations. With no evidence of regulated data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF B is configured to process PHI or EU PII, residency and retention controls become relevant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Review retention settings if sensitive data is added.
